name: v0.3.25 fresh transfer of the frozen episode-drain candidate
research_question: Does the frozen v0.3.24 episode-drain candidate transfer to new application graphs that were not used to design or repair it, while preserving Guard-confirmed bugs and the episode-drain safety invariants?
not: another inspected repair of Campus or Studio
permission to edit the v0.3.24 candidate
permission to change the product default
permission to pick a favorable graph after seeing policy results
topology_rule: New positives are a single spine plus one board workflow. They are not the v0.3.20 dual mid/child column graph. Negatives reuse the v0.3.20 catalog and kiosk qualification classes on new page sets.

positive_requires: at least two distinct child-workflow chains that cross the horizon
at least one finding-return opportunity with two eligible buttons
at least one horizon-only return path of length 3
at least one nested handoff edge
qualification.shelf_requires: catalog class: no nested chain, no handoff, max branch depth below 3
qualification.counter_requires: kiosk class: no nested chain, no handoff, at least two finding-return opportunities and one horizon-only path

outcomes.C: freeze or protocol mismatch, candidate edit, Guard bug loss on any fresh target, historical Guard loss, episode advance without relocation, cross-hub invalidation, restore probe, nested handoff on a negative control, app-specific candidate logic, or product default change
outcomes.D: safety holds but fewer than 3 positive targets are structurally evaluable at budget 120
outcomes.B: safety and Guard preservation hold, at least 3 positives are evaluable, but fewer than 3 keep every Guard bug while reaching the preregistered structure
outcomes.A: the frozen candidate is evaluable on at least 3 of 4 new positives, preserves Guard bugs on all 6 new targets and the historical suite, keeps both negative controls free of nested handoff, and does not change the product default

evaluable: At budget 120 the candidate records a nested handoff, a local drain, a finding-gated return drain, or a residual-debt relocation, and it also records a completed or returned sequence.
phase_order: generator, static qualification, and suite freeze
publish the derived outcome without tuning
